Reviewer feedback and the changes we made

For each comment: the issue, the reviewer’s feedback, the screen before, and the fixed screen with the steps to try it. Live prototype: https://cruz-new.vercel.app.

How to read this. There are two rounds. Round 1 (Oct 12) is feedback from Oshada and Akila on the first build (Oct 10). Round 2 (Oct 13) is the Figma board comments, compared with the build after round 1. Screenshots are cropped to the part of the screen the comment is about, and are inside this file, so it works on its own. Venue settings in the prototype last for the current browser tab only. Live links work once the latest changes are deployed.

Round 1 in detail

1. Move the “changes apply to new payouts only” note next to Save

Venue SettingsOshada (Venue Settings feedback, item 1)

Issue

The note sat in a paragraph under the heading, a full screen away from Save. Someone pressing Save would not have it in view, so the effect of saving was easy to miss.

Feedback

Move the “changes apply to new payouts only” note near the Save button so users understand the impact before saving.

First build

After the feedback

Workflow after the change

  1. Open Manage, then Venues, and select a venue.
  2. Change any setting, for example turn Cheque on.
  3. Look at the buttons at the bottom: “Changes apply to new payouts only. Submitted payouts are not affected.” sits directly above Cancel and Save.
  4. Select Save. A confirmation message appears, and reloading the page shows the saved values.

Open live: Venue Settings (Super Admin view)

Changed in: VenueSettingsForm

2. Toggles: clear label, state announced, keyboard, state shown in text

Venue SettingsOshada (Venue Settings feedback, item 2)

Issue

The switch was already a real switch control with a label and a visible focus ring, but its state was shown only by colour (blue or grey). Nothing said On or Off in words, and the explanation under each title was not linked to the switch for screen readers.

Feedback

Ensure each toggle has a clear label, announces its on/off state, and works with a keyboard. Show the state in text where it helps users understand the impact.

First build

After the feedback

Workflow after the change

  1. Open a venue. Each switch now has the word On or Off beside it.
  2. Press Tab to reach a switch. A focus ring appears.
  3. Press Space or Enter to switch it. The word and the colour change together.
  4. A screen reader reads the method name, On or Off, and the line of description under the title.
  5. Turning Payment File for Your Bank on reveals Venue Code. Turning Cheque on reveals the question about who can enter cheque details. Turning either off hides its extra settings.

Open live: Venue Settings (Super Admin view)

Changed in: Switch, PaymentMethodRow

3. Shorter descriptions, detail only when needed

Venue SettingsOshada (Venue Settings feedback, item 3) and Akila

Issue

Every card carried a full sentence or two of explanation, the page opened with a paragraph before any control, and the cheque question and its three options were long. The page took a lot of reading for a screen with three settings.

Feedback

Reduce reading time with brief descriptions and reveal extra detail only when needed. For example: Funds transfer — Always available; Bank payment file — On/off; Cheque — On/off. Keep the venue-code note (“Included in the file; leading zeros are kept”) and shorten the cheque question to Who can enter cheque details? (Akila: try to make it less wordy if possible, no need to mention everything, too much text here.)

First build

After the feedback

Workflow after the change

  1. Open a venue. The intro paragraph under “How Winners Are Paid” is gone.
  2. Each method has one short line: Funds Transfer “Paid into the winner’s bank account automatically.”, Payment File for Your Bank “Your team uploads a payment file to your bank’s online portal.”, Cheque “Winners are paid by cheque.”
  3. Turn Payment File for Your Bank on. Venue Code appears with “Included in the file; leading zeros are kept.”
  4. Turn Cheque on. The question reads “Who can enter cheque details?” with three one-line options: Collector Only, Authoriser Only, Collector and Authoriser Both.
  5. Turn them off again and the extra settings disappear.

Open live: Venue Settings (Super Admin view)

Changed in: VenueSettingsForm, venue-data (option text), ChequeModeOptions

4. Funds Transfer looks like something you can switch

Venue SettingsOshada (Venue Settings feedback, item 4, optional)

Issue

Funds Transfer used the same white card as the two methods that have switches, with no switch. A reader could think it was missing a control, or that it could be turned off.

Feedback

Funds Transfer is always available, but its card looks configurable. Label it Always available or style it differently. (Follow-up from the team: keep it looking like the other cards, with a clear Always available badge.)

First build

After the feedback

Workflow after the change

  1. Open a venue. Funds Transfer is the same white card as the other two.
  2. Where the others have a switch, it has a green “Always available” badge, so it is clear there is nothing to turn on or off.
  3. The two cards below it, Payment File for Your Bank and Cheque, keep their switches.

Open live: Venue Settings (Super Admin view)

Changed in: AlwaysAvailableMethodRow (new)

5. “Cheque Details Entered By” shows the actual username

Approver and Authoriser review (Payment Method Details card)Oshada (Payout Summary)

Issue

The row showed the venue setting (for example “Collector and Authoriser Both”). That says who is allowed to enter the details, not who did, so it could not tell a reviewer who to ask about a cheque.

Feedback

Cheque Details Entered By: Should be populated by the actual username other than the available options.

First build

After the feedback

Workflow after the change

  1. Open the Authoriser review with the Cheque: Collector and Authoriser payout.
  2. Cheque Details Entered By shows M.Santos (Collector), because the Collector entered the cheque number.
  3. Enter the missing Cheque Name and select Validate Cheque.
  4. The row now reads M.Santos (Collector), R.Nguyen (Authoriser). If nobody has entered details yet, it reads Not entered yet.
  5. With Cheque: Authoriser Only it goes from Not entered yet to R.Nguyen (Authoriser). With Cheque: Collector Only it shows M.Santos (Collector) and the details are read-only. The Approver sees the same row, read-only.

Open live: Authoriser review, Cheque: Collector and Authoriser

Changed in: RecordedDestination, AuthoriserPayoutView, payout-review-scenarios

6. Details the Authoriser enters fill the card, no new placeholders

Authoriser review (Payment Method Details card)Oshada (Authoriser entry)

Issue

The card first listed “Not entered yet” for the cheque number and name, with a separate form underneath. After the Authoriser checked the details, the values appeared in a second block, so the same two labels were on screen twice and the first pair still said Not entered yet.

Feedback

When the cheque details are entered by Authoriser, the details should be populated in the card instead of showing new placeholders.

First build

After the feedback

Workflow after the change

  1. Open the Authoriser review with the Cheque: Authoriser Only payout.
  2. Under Payment Method Details, Cheque Details Entered By says Not entered yet, and the Cheque Number and Cheque Name fields sit inside the card. There is no separate form.
  3. Enter both and select Validate Cheque. Leaving one empty shows a message under that field.
  4. The values now fill the card (Cheque Number, Cheque Name) with “Cheque bearer name matches.” and an edit pencil. Cheque Details Entered By shows R.Nguyen (Authoriser). The second screenshot is the Collector and Authoriser payout, where the card lists both people.
  5. Tick the confirmation box. Authorise is now available. Selecting the pencil reopens the fields and switches Authorise off until the details are checked again.

Open live: Authoriser review, Cheque: Authoriser Only

Changed in: ChequeDetailsEditor, RecordedDestination, AuthoriserPayoutView

7. A switched-off method sends the Collector straight to Payment Breakdown

Collector flow (MBT-10, CHE-07)Oshada (on MBT-10)

Issue

When the venue turned off the method the Collector had chosen, the Collector still opened Payment Method Details, saw a warning there and a disabled Next, and had to find their own way back to choose again. The screen they landed on was one they could not use.

Feedback

Instead of opening the Payment Method Details page, showing the warning and taking the collector directly to the Payment Breakdown would be ideal.

First build

After the feedback

Workflow after the change

  1. A Collector chooses a way to pay the rest on Payment Breakdown, for example Payment File for Your Bank, and continues through the steps.
  2. Meanwhile an Admin switches that method off for the venue (Manage, Venues, turn it off, Save).
  3. The Collector reaches the Payment Method Details step.
  4. They are sent straight back to Payment Breakdown. A warning at the top says “Payment File for Your Bank is no longer available at this venue. Choose another way to pay the rest.”
  5. How the Rest Is Paid lists only the methods still available. The earlier choice is cleared. In this prototype the amounts typed on Payment Breakdown are not kept.

Open live: Collector, Payment Breakdown (switch the method off at the venue first)

Changed in: PayoutDestinationDetailsForm, PaymentBreakdownForm, collector-data

Round 2 in detail

R2-1. Heading, names and one-line descriptions on Venue Settings

Venue SettingsPromptLane (Figma)

Issue

The section was called “How Winners Are Paid” with no explanation line, the descriptions spoke to the reader (“Your team uploads a payment file to your bank’s online portal”) and described an action rather than the method, and the two methods used longer names.

Feedback

i feel Payouts configuration is a better title. desc: “Choose how winners can be paid” remove last 2 sentences. agree with oshadha on adding changes applied to new payouts only message when saving. • descriptions overall should be concise. let’s not use “you”/“your” a lot. • Manual bank transfer is better. desc: is it needed to mention what is done with this here instead of describing what it is. • Instead of Funds transfer EFT (Electronic Funds Transfer) is better imo. • agree with oshadha on always available style. can have a disabled toggle set to On.

Note

Names: the team chose Electronic Fund Transfer (written in full, not EFT) and Manual Bank Transfer. The comment on the always-available card is followed: the card now has a disabled switch set to On, and the “Always available” badge was removed at the team’s request.

Before

After the Figma comments

Workflow after the change

  1. Open Manage, then Venues, and select a venue.
  2. The section is called “Payouts configuration”, with “Choose how winners can be paid.” under it.
  3. Electronic Fund Transfer has a switch that is fixed to On and cannot be changed. Manual Bank Transfer and Cheque have On/Off switches.
  4. Each method has one line that says what it is, for example “Paid by uploading a payment file to the bank’s online portal.”
  5. The same names appear in the Venues list, the Collector’s “How the Rest Is Paid” list and the review pages.

Open live: Venue Settings (Super Admin view)

Changed in: VenueSettingsForm, AlwaysAvailableMethodRow, Switch, venue-data (names)

R2-2. Simpler lines for the cheque options

Venue SettingsPromptLane (Figma)

Issue

Each option line was longer than it needed to be and used “The” and “Either” where a short sentence does the job.

Feedback

make descriptions simpler: Collector Only: Collector enters the cheque details. Authoriser can view them. Authoriser Only: Authoriser enters the cheque details. Collector and Authoriser: Both can enter and edit the cheque details. • here something like “Cheque detail entry” with a desc like Select who can enter the cheque details.

Note

Not adopted: the label “Cheque detail entry”. Oshada had already asked for the question “Who can enter cheque details?”, so that stays.

Before

After the Figma comments

Workflow after the change

  1. Turn Cheque on. The question reads “Who can enter cheque details?”.
  2. Collector Only: “Collector enters the cheque details. Authoriser can view them.”
  3. Authoriser Only: “Authoriser enters the cheque details.”
  4. Collector and Authoriser Both: “Both can enter and edit the cheque details.”

Open live: Venue Settings (Super Admin view)

Changed in: venue-data (option text)

Venue SettingsPromptLane (Figma)

make the buttons consistent to other designs. refer to collector view?

After the Figma comments

Approver and Authoriser review (Payment Method Details card)PromptLane (Figma)

saying paid by here is confusing. what about “Method: Manual bank transfer”? • shall we make not entered yet a different color so its noticeable? check how similar scenarios are shown in the system

R2-6. Authoriser entry: required fields, one short hint, “Check Name Match”

Authoriser review (Payment Method Details card)PromptLane (Figma)

Issue

The page showed a two-sentence warning telling the Authoriser where to enter the details, the fields did not say they were required, and “Validate Cheque” did not say what is being checked.

Feedback

“Enter cheque details” is enough here i think. how it’s needed when authorising is shown when trying to authorise without entering data right? also make this fields mandatory (asterick) • here we discussed validate cheque is misleading right? let’s go with “Check Name Match” (this comment has 2 replies and an image that could not be read)

Note

Authorise stays disabled until both details are entered and checked, as agreed. The short line explains why.

Before

After the Figma comments

Workflow after the change

  1. Open the Authoriser review with the Cheque: Authoriser Only payout.
  2. Cheque Number and Cheque Name have a red asterisk.
  3. Above the buttons one line says “Enter cheque details before authorising.”
  4. Enter both and select “Check Name Match”. The values fill the card and the line disappears.
  5. Tick the confirmation box. Authorise is now available. The Collector’s cheque screen uses the same button name.

did they ask for a description here? feels unnecessary • no need to have this description i think. fields mention they are optional, otherwise its repetitive • i feel like this text is not needed here since the button says what it does

R2-9. Return dialog: direct text, required reason, character limit

Approver and Authoriser reviewPromptLane (Figma)

Issue

The dialog used a long description, did not show that the reason is required, had no limit, and the placeholder started with “For example”. A very long reason would also have been hard to show on the Collector’s page.

Feedback

make the description direct and clear. reason is mandatory right? add the asterick. also does it have a character limit? if yes, is it scrollable? no need to say “For example” in the placeholder • (on the returned payout) if reason doesn’t have a character limit, we have to be mindful how the reason is shown here

Note

Not adopted: dropping the role from “returned by D.Walsh (Approver)”. The stories say both the Approver and the Authoriser can return a payout.

Before

After the Figma comments

Workflow after the change

  1. Open any review page and select Return for Correction.
  2. The dialog says “Enter the reason for returning this payout. The Collector will see it.”
  3. Reason has a red asterisk and the placeholder reads “The BSB does not match the account name.”
  4. The box allows 500 characters, shows a count (0/500), and scrolls if the text is long.
  5. Selecting Return Payout with an empty reason shows “Enter a reason before returning the payout.”
  6. On the Collector’s correction page the reason wraps inside the message.

Open live: Authoriser review, then Return for Correction

Changed in: ReturnForCorrectionDialog, return-payout (limit), WarningAlert (wrapping), FormField
